name: Werewolfmaxxing

card.summary: A style-focused look that combines tall, lean, muscular build, healthy skin and grown-out body and facial hair to project a wild, high-testosterone 'werewolf' aura.
card.note: A style archetype from forum culture; its stated requirements, such as a minimum height, are community opinion.

quick.overview:
Werewolfmaxxing is a looksmaxxing style built on the werewolf as an archetype of masculine appeal. A looksmax.org guide describes it as an animalistic, wolf-like aura that its author says fulfills a female fantasy, and presents it as a bundle of traits [1].

The guide's list covers height, a lean muscular physique at about 8 to 12 percent body fat, clean and hydrated skin, and the grown-out hair that gives the look its name. The guide cites Jacob Black from Twilight, played by Taylor Lautner, as a reference point [1].
quick.how: Followers combine ordinary looksmaxxing basics, such as leanness, training and skin care, with letting body and facial hair grow out into a thick, wild style. One looksmax.org reply to the guide jokes that all teeth except the canines should be shaved down, and another asks whether it is simply looksmaxxing [1].
quick.risks: No health risks are specific to the style itself. The guide's absolute rule that the look is closed to anyone under 6'0 is its author's opinion, and some commenters question whether it differs from general looksmaxxing [1].

lead: Werewolfmaxxing is a looksmaxxing style archetype in which a man aims to look like a werewolf: tall, lean and muscular, with a rugged, hairy, high-testosterone presence. The main written description is a looksmax.org thread titled as an ultimate guide, which states that werewolves are among the biggest female fantasy archetypes and that the guide shows how to achieve an animalistic aura to match [1].

The guide lists requirements in numbered steps. Height comes first, with the author stating that the look needs 6'0 (183 cm) or more and citing Taylor Lautner's Jacob Black in Twilight, whose appeal the author says was criticized when his short height showed. Next is physique at 8 to 12 percent body fat, anywhere from lean athletic to muscular, with footballer Robert Lewandowski and Austin Dunham named as examples. Skin must be clean, hydrated and healthy [1].

The hair component, which gives the style its name, involves growing out facial and body hair for a wilder look. Community replies treat the idea semi-humorously, with one joking about shaving all teeth but the canines and another noting that it amounts to looksmaxxing done in a certain way [1].

chain: Height, leanness and muscle build a strong frame
Healthy skin and grown-out hair add a wild, rugged look
angle.text: Practitioners use the werewolf as a template for a rugged masculine look: lean and muscular with healthy skin and natural hair. It assembles standard looksmaxxing traits under one aesthetic.

infobox: Height, 8-12% body fat, clean skin, wild hair
Taylor Lautner as Jacob Black, Robert Lewandowski

paras: The guide's author argues the style needs more than hair. The numbered list starts with height and says anyone below 6'0 should instead pursue heightmaxxing, then physique, then skin [1]. The author says leanness gives sharper facial features and a more toned body [1].

Replies range from jokes, such as shaving all teeth except the canines, to the question of whether werewolfmaxxing is just looksmaxxing. The guide author's answer is that it is looksmaxxing aimed at a certain archetype [1].

lore.intro: Werewolfmaxxing is discussed on looksmax.org as an archetype-based style guide [1].

claims.claim: The werewolf archetype is a top female fantasy, so matching it increases appeal.
claims.believers: The guide's author says werewolves are among the biggest female fantasy archetypes and that the look fulfills them [1].
claims.experts: No published studies have tested the werewolf archetype as an attractiveness strategy.

claims.claim: The look is only available at 6'0 or above.
claims.believers: The author says a man below 183 cm cannot be 'werewolfmaxxed' and cites Lautner's reception as an example [1].
claims.experts: No published studies have examined a height cutoff for this style.
